title: Runway, SLA & Cost Accountability — Customer QBR
summary: Monthly QBR-style health check focusing on runway (commit vs burst), SLA alignment, and cost accountability. Agreed to run a 1-week production trace benchmark, share detailed cost-breakdown by route, and schedule a security deep-dive for SSO/KMS questions. Customer wants a 3% latency improvement target on critical endpoints or quantified fallback plan.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Aisha Malik (Kairo Head of ML), Roberto Diaz (Kairo VP Eng), Jen Nguyen (Kairo FinOps), Samir Patel (Kairo SRE), Dana Ortiz (Kairo Procurement)

Auto-summary: QBR-style checkin — covered usage, cost, SLA, roadmap; agreed to bench run and security deep-dive.

[00:00] Ethan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll try to keep to an hour, lots to go over, quick intros if anyone new?
[00:12] Aisha Malik: hi all, Aisha here, running ML at Kairo — glad we're doing the fiscal and stability review together.
[00:18] Roberto Diaz: Roberto, VP Eng, focusing on reliability.
[00:22] Jen Nguyen: Jen, FinOps, here to dig into costs.
[00:26] Priya Rao: Priya from Redwood, I'm your SE on optimization and batching.
[00:29] Liam Chen: Liam, CSM, will help coordinate follow-ups.
[00:32] Samir Patel: Samir, SRE. we've seen spikes last month around 11/9 that caused some throttling.
[00:37] Ethan Park: cool, quick agenda, 1) usage & runway 2) SLA and oncall gaps 3) cost hotspots 4) roadmap ask + next steps.
[00:45] Aisha Malik: one housekeeping, our board asked for a 90-day cost forecast with base + burst, so we'll need some clear numbers.
[00:53] Jen Nguyen: yes, and show us per-route token unit economics — embeddings are killing us in the last mile.
[00:59] [01:02] Priya Rao: noted — embeddings vs generation is often the biggest delta; we can show you batch vs streaming costs and where caching helps.
[01:12] Ethan Park: quick snapshot from Redwood side — usage has grown 38% month over month for Kairo this quarter, burst events cause 4-6x token increase for a few hours. we flagged the top three endpoints: query-summarize, rerank-topk, and user-profile-embed.
[01:28] Samir Patel: that matches our telemetry — rerank spikes correlate with nightly batch traffic and a downstream retry loop.
[01:36] Roberto Diaz: question — when we hit Dedicated capacity, how predictable is latency? last incident the fallback to hosted added 150 ms p50, which is getting us close to SLA.
[01:47] Priya Rao: right, Dedicated gives predictable throughput but we recommend canary policies and automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants. fallback can add overhead depending on model variant and KV-cache warm state.
[01:59] [02:09] Aisha Malik: can you explain KV-cache warm state, just a simple description for execs?
[02:14] Priya Rao: sure, KV-cache stores key/value states for transformer decoding so when you switch models or cold-start the cache is empty — it builds up as tokens stream which can add latency for the initial requests. our continuous-batching and persistent cache options reduce that.
[02:32] Jen Nguyen: is there a cost to keeping the cache hot? like memory/slots?
[02:36] Priya Rao: moderate; cache residency uses GPU memory and can limit concurrent model instances. you trade off footprint vs token-level latency/cost. we can show a cost curve.
[02:48] [03:01] Liam Chen: quick poll — which SLA levers matter most? availability (uptime), p99 latency, or sustained throughput?
[03:08] Roberto Diaz: p99 latency for our interactive flows, availability for API ingestion. throughput is secondary.
[03:12] Aisha Malik: agreed on p99, because small latency spikes degrade UX and our user retention.
[03:16] Dana Ortiz: procurement wants defined credits for burst; can we get a burst buffer priced?
[03:21] Ethan Park: yes we have Dedicated burst buffer options — pricing addendum can be drafted if you confirm desired headroom.
[03:28] Jen Nguyen: give me an example number — what's the delta if we reserve 2x baseline for 2 hours/day?
[03:34] Priya Rao: rough rule of thumb — reserve capacity costs ~60% of overcommit costs but reduces overage at a lower unit price; we'll produce an annotated spreadsheet.
[03:41] [04:00] Samir Patel: security questions — we need SOC2 details, audit log retention, and KMS integration. any gotchas with Private?
[04:09] Priya Rao: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs with configurable retention, and SAML/SSO. there are network requirements for VPC peering; our on-prem package adds additional review steps.
[04:24] Roberto Diaz: does Private change performance characteristics? we worry about variability across sites.
[04:29] Priya Rao: typically Private has more consistent network latency but your hardware choice matters; our runtime can be tuned, but quantization/compilation paths may differ. small model variants may be preferable for edge private installs.
[04:44] [05:05] Aisha Malik: back to cost, our embeddings bill went up 42% — any quick wins to reduce embed cost?
[05:11] Priya Rao: yes — suggestions: 1) batch embedding requests to increase throughput 2) reuse cached vectors where semantics allow 3) consider smaller embedding models for lower-value features 4) downsample or pre-filter using cheaper heuristics.
[05:26] Jen Nguyen: can Redwood provide an automated suggestion engine?
[05:30] Priya Rao: Redwood Optimize includes recommendations; we can run a one-off analysis if you share traffic samples.
[05:38] [06:00] Ethan Park: proposal: Redwood runs a 1-week trace benchmark (non-prod mirror of traffic) to report p99, KV-cache hit rates, and per-route cost breakdown. does Kairo have a traffic sample we can mirror?
[06:10] Aisha Malik: yes, we'll export a week of anonymized tps and percentiles. can we mask PII?
[06:15] Priya Rao: absolutely — we accept anonymized traces. we'll also exclude user content.
[06:19] Samir Patel: timeline?
[06:21] Liam Chen: target start next Monday and finish in 7 days, deliverable a PDF + spreadsheet.
[06:26] Jen Nguyen: ok. and for the SLA target, can Redwood propose a 3% p99 improvement plan or fallback plan?
[06:32] Priya Rao: we can propose optimizations: persistent KV cache, smaller quantized variants for cold paths, and route-level batching. we'll include expected delta and confidence range.
[06:40] [07:05] Roberto Diaz: about rollouts — if you deploy a new model version, how do we avoid regressions? we need canary and automatic rollback.
[07:12] Priya Rao: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B by traffic %, automatic fallback to previous model if quality or latency regressions breach thresholds. you can pin customers or routes.
[07:21] Aisha Malik: quality monitoring: can we tie evaluation prompts to detect regressions?
[07:25] Priya Rao: yes — Redwood Optimize can run prompt evals against new variants; alerts can be tied to prompt sets.
[07:32] [08:00] Ethan Park: quick interruption — procurement question, what's minimum commitment for Dedicated to get a meaningful discount?
[08:08] Dana Ortiz: (from customer) yes that's our angle.
[08:11] Ethan Park: typical is 6-12 month reserved capacity; discounts scale with commit. we'll draft a tiered proposal in the pricing addendum.
[08:19] Jen Nguyen: prefer numbers in the addendum please — show 3 scenarios: baseline, baseline+20% reserve, baseline+100% burst buffer.
[08:26] [09:00] Priya Rao: rough ballpark we can provide now, but will prefer the cost spreadsheet after bench run to give accurate token-level unit prices per route.
[09:08] Samir Patel: operationally, when failover to hosted occurs we saw 5% error rate increase — can Redwood provide more graceful degradation policies?
[09:16] Priya Rao: yes — circuit breaking, degraded model variants, and queue shedding are options. we can configure timeouts and fallbacks per route.
[09:26] Aisha Malik: that sounds good. also we want better observability on token-level costing by endpoint for finance.
[09:33] Liam Chen: we'll provide token-level breakdown by route and a visualization for execs.
[09:38] [10:02] Roberto Diaz: can you show us what the prioritization would look like if we had to pick three optimization levers?
[10:08] Priya Rao: 1) KV-cache + persistent warm nodes for interactive critical flows, 2) quantized model variants for cold/batch paths, 3) route-level batching for embeddings. we'll quantify cost reduction and expected latency impact in the report.
[10:21] Jen Nguyen: competitors — we've talked to Vendor X and they promised simpler pricing but they didn't have KV caching. just context.
[10:28] Ethan Park: good to know — Redwood's differentiation is observability and predictable economics across modes.
[10:33] [11:00] Aisha Malik: security deep-dive — we need SSO integration and proof of audit logs for SOC2. can Redwood vendor questionnaire be filled?
[11:06] Liam Chen: yes we'll send the vendor security packet, SOC2 report redacted, and schedule a 45-min security call.
[11:11] Dana Ortiz: ideal timeframe week of Dec 6.
[11:14] Ethan Park: we'll book that.
[11:17] [12:00] Priya Rao: small technical note — if we'll mirror traffic for benching, include distribution by payload size and percent of streaming responses vs non-streaming. streaming affects batching behavior.
[12:29] Samir Patel: noted, we'll extract that from our logs.
[12:34] [13:00] Jen Nguyen: ask — can Redwood credit our account for one week of bench usage? it helps us justify pilot cost.
[13:07] Ethan Park: we can make a pilot credit case; I'll escalate with finance.
[13:12] Liam Chen: I'll include that in the follow-up email.
[13:18] [14:00] Aisha Malik: on roadmap alignment, we plan model rollout in Q1; we want to coordinate canary windows and capacity reservation.
[14:08] Priya Rao: recommend reserving some Dedicated capacity for Q1 and plan a phased canary with rollback thresholds.
[14:15] Roberto Diaz: and set up a joint runbook for outages.
[14:18] Ethan Park: agreed, runbook draft will be in the follow-up.
[14:22] [15:00] Dana Ortiz: procurement will need contract T&Cs for burst and audit clauses. can you provide a sample?
[15:06] Ethan Park: yes, we'll send sample terms with the pricing addendum.
[15:11] [16:00] Priya Rao: last technical note — we noticed one route with unusually low kv-hit rate; might be due to varying prompt prefixes. consider normalizing prompts where possible. small change, big win.
[16:23] Aisha Malik: good tip, we'll try a normalizer in preprocessing.
[16:29] [17:00] Liam Chen: recap and next steps: Redwood to run bench, share cost spreadsheet and pricing addendum, schedule security deep-dive, customer to share traffic sample and critical endpoints.
[17:12] Jen Nguyen: target dates please?
[17:15] Liam Chen: bench results by Dec 6, pricing addendum draft Dec 10, security call week of Dec 6.
[17:22] Ethan Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the deliverables.
[17:27] [18:00] Meeting ends.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-attributions, filler words preserved, minor transcription artifacts (e.g., "V P C" vs "VPC"), natural speech pacing and brief crosstalk present.
